summary.headline: Clean Max Q1 FY27 PAT rose to INR55 crore on revenue more than doubling to INR832 crore; FY28 EBITDA guided at minimum INR3,000 crore.
summary.overview: Revenue from operations rose 107% YoY to INR832 crore, with RE power sales up 47% to INR528 crore and RE services jumping to INR300 crore from INR41 crore. Reported EBITDA rose 68% to INR462 crore (adjusted INR494 crore, up about 74% on a cash basis), and PAT reached INR55 crore. Management added about 500 MW of capacity in the quarter and issued its first FY28 EBITDA guidance of a minimum INR3,000 crore, with steady-state net debt of about INR16,000 crore. Near-term headwinds include a roughly 70% curtailment at the Bikaner CTU project, which management expects to persist through FY27.

financial_highlights.change: +47% YoY (vs INR358 crore in prior-year quarter)
vs INR41 crore in prior-year quarter (about 6x)

segments.name: RE power sales
segments.commentary: Revenue INR528 crore, up 47% YoY; EBITDA margin 84% vs 76% a year earlier. Gross margin flat at about 92-93%, with expansion driven by SG&A falling as a share of income. Of total quarterly EBITDA, about INR334 crore came from assets operational for the full prior 12 months.

segments.name: RE services (C&I EPC and O&M)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR300 crore vs INR41 crore a year earlier; EBITDA margin 11.2%. Order book of 147 MW contracted and under execution, with management saying order-to-execution is within 12 months.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of the deferral of ALMM List-II (cells) and whether the company can benefit.
qa_highlights.answer: Projects commissioned before 31 December can use domestic modules with imported cells, saving about INR60 lakh per MW; company is pulling forward some Maharashtra and Karnataka brownfield STU builds, and no module contract is signed yet.

qa_highlights.question: Can capacity by BESS bay for the Koppal CTU project be broken out, and is the March 2027 second bay a risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not have the split on hand; said BESS have spare evacuation capacity and fungibility across the two bays, so a slight delay in the second bay should not break the 1.5 GW target.

qa_highlights.question: Why did debenture holders get a security cover change from 0.7x to 1x?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the trust deed allowed a range of 0.7x to 1.25x; the company fixed it at 1x for consistency with the planned corporate bond, not an increase.

qa_highlights.question: Battery storage: how it plays into business and whether new PPAs include batteries.
qa_highlights.answer: Company has greenlit a first BESS STU project in Rajasthan, signed MOUs with three clients in the last month, and sees three C&I use cases; BESS-as-a-Service tariff uplift estimated at INR3-4/unit excluding generation cost.

qa_highlights.question: Curtailment impact on EBITDA and quarterly generation/PLF detail.
qa_highlights.answer: Management estimates the Bikaner CTU project is 13% of run-rate EBITDA; at 70% curtailment that is about INR170 crore on a full-year basis; EBITDA would be about 8-9% higher without it. PLF given on trailing 12 months basis only.

qa_highlights.question: Competitive threat from Adani, Reliance and NTPC entering C&I, and why hyperscalers keep choosing CleanMax.
qa_highlights.answer: Management cites 15 years of C&I focus, 600+ customers with 80% of new volume from repeat clients, multi-state wind-plus-solar footprint, and a fragmented market where it holds about 14% share.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 3,000 crore FY28 EBITDA guidance corporate-level, and what is the peak debt?
qa_highlights.answer: Guidance is corporate-level, including RE services; steady-state net debt corresponding to INR3,000 crore EBITDA is about INR16,000 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Sustainability of growth: can the company repeat contracted capacity growth of about 4,000 MW over the next two years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it can meet or exceed about 4,000 MW of contracted additions over two years, but tripling is not feasible given execution limits; organisational gaps in five to six areas were reviewed with the board.

guidance_outlook: FY28 minimum reported EBITDA guided at about INR3,000 crore, nearly 2.3-2.4x FY26 EBITDA of about INR1,290 crore; first-ever forward EBITDA guidance, corporate level including RE services.
Steady-state net debt corresponding to INR3,000 crore EBITDA put at about INR16,000 crore.
Minimum operational opex capacity of 4,600 MW expected by 1 April 2027 (3,100 MW at start of FY27 plus about 1,500 MW to be added in FY27).

FY27 capacity addition guidance of at least 1.5 GW reaffirmed; 400-500 MW added in Q1 FY27 with plenty of unbuilt capacity; Koppal CTU project cited as 543 MW contributor with commissioning by October 2026 and March 2027.

Bikaner CTU curtailment of about 70% expected to persist through FY27; management says to assume heavy curtailment for the rest of the fiscal. Company estimates about INR170 crore full-year EBITDA impact on a 13% CTU share of run-rate EBITDA of INR1,870 crore.
Run-rate EBITDA not published quarterly; management guides that year-end run-rate EBITDA is typically 1x to 1.1x the next year's reported EBITDA.
capex_capacity: Contracted capacity about 6 GW as of 30 June 2026: 3.5 GW operational in RE power sales and about 2.5 GW contracted and under execution.
RE services: 682 MW operational after 127 MW commissioned in Q1; 147 MW contracted and under execution.
Q1 FY27 commissioning about 500 MW total: about 400 MW RE power sales and slightly above 100 MW RE services.
Trailing 12-month capacity addition about 1,740-1,743 MW, up from 450 MW a year earlier; CTU build pace around one site a year, roughly 500 MW per year.
Management did not disclose Q1 capex; breakup of fixed asset growth to be provided offline. Gross block INR14,138 crore.
BESS: first BESS investment greenlit (STU project in Rajasthan), about 2-hour storage; not material to FY27 capex; MOUs signed with three clients in the past month.
Grid uptime above 99% in STU; STU plus rooftop about 87% of EBITDA; trailing-12-month PLFs stable to marginally improved in wind, similar in solar and hybrid.
demand_pricing: Data and AI customers are 42% of contracted capacity, grown about 10x from March 2024 to March 2026; about 35% share of hyperscaler business in India per management; new hyperscaler deals announced in calendar 2026 with Meta, Apple, Google and Amazon.

Industrial (C&I, non-Data and AI) is 58% of contracted volumes; contracted volumes doubled in two years (about 46% CAGR); about 600 unique C&I customers across 10 states, 7 where power is being evacuated and 3 more contracted.
Around 75-80% of new contracts are with existing clients; about 80% of volumes with AA/AAA/multinational-rated customers; PPA tenure averages 23 years.
Tariff: operating portfolio about INR3.93/unit; 2.5 GW under-construction contracted book about INR4/unit (up from INR3.85 per an analyst's quote), without storage.
Average C&I PPA size about 13 MW; hyperscaler CTU deals about 200-250 MW average; largest STU contract about 150 MW.
Market share in C&I about 14% (from 12%), per management citing recent statistics; ~7% of industrial power in India sourced via bilateral green.
RE services: order book 147 MW; order-to-execution within 12 months; revenue from EPC margins plus O&M annuity.
Q1 unallocated EBITDA of INR31 crore, per accounting segment allocation with auditors KPMG.
risks_watch: Bikaner CTU curtailment (about 70%) persisting through FY27; resolution timing unknown per management.
Execution pace: FY27 1.5 GW target depends on Koppal CTU bays (October 2026 and March 2027) and pulling forward brownfield projects before the 31 December ALMM cut-off.
Module procurement pricing not yet contracted; ALMM-2 deferral benefit (about INR60 lakh/MW) is limited to projects commissioned by 31 December.
Rising competition from Adani, Reliance and NTPC in C&I; hyperscaler market share (35%) expected to decline as market grows.
Net debt rising to INR11,809 crore from INR9,684 crore in Q1; INR4,483 crore debt tied to under-construction assets; first domestic bond pending.
Tamil Nadu approvals had 1-2 months of flux after government change, now said to be resolving.
key_quotes: So, we are in an almost happy situation to be supply-constrained, not demand-constrained.
we are comfortable providing that new guidance, that we will have a minimum EBITDA of INR3,000 crores in FY28
So, you cannot sign what you cannot execute, else you lose your trust with clients.
So, it's not a winner-takes-all market, this is a highly fragmented market, even a market leader like us has 14% or so market share.
summary.management_tone: Confident and forward-leaning on growth, FY28 guidance and data-centre demand, while openly acknowledging the Bikaner curtailment and execution gaps; answers on BESS and capex were partly deferred to offline follow-up.
